summary: Frontend-only mobile-responsive pass on the /watch end-user surface (Browse, Live TV, Movies, Series, Search, Watchlist, Favorites, Player) at 390x844 and 1280x800. Case-insensitive USER login (TEST/12345) regression also re-verified. 24 of 26 UI checks pass; one real responsive bug found on /watch Browse during data loading.

ui_bugs.issue: Horizontal page scroll on mobile 390px. document.documentElement.scrollWidth=844 (body scrolls right ~454px). Root cause: the Row component's LOADING state (Watch.js lines 183-187) renders <div className='flex gap-3'> with 6 shrink-0 cards (w-32 = 128px each ≈ 768px+ total) and is MISSING overflow-x-auto. The loaded state (line 209) correctly has overflow-x-auto. So while data is loading (or any time the queries are pending), /watch overflows horizontally. Confirmed by probe: navMobile is contained (clientW=390, scrollW=657 inside), Live TV/Movies/Series/Search/Watchlist/Favorites all have docW=390 (no overflow). Only /watch Browse is affected.
ui_bugs.selector: Row loading state: flex gap-3 children w-32 h-48 sm:w-44 sm:h-64 shrink-0 (Watch.js:183-187)
ui_bugs.fix_suggestion: Add `overflow-x-auto scrollbar-thin -mx-4 sm:-mx-2 px-4 sm:px-2` to the loading skeleton's inner flex div so the loading state matches the loaded state's containment. OR add `overflow-x-hidden` to the <main> in WatchShell (Watch.js:96) as a defensive guard.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The only real UI bug is the Row loading-skeleton on /watch Browse causing horizontal overflow on 390px mobile (scrollWidth=844 vs clientWidth=390). After the main agent adds overflow-x-auto to the skeleton flex div at Watch.js:183 (or overflow-x-hidden to <main> at Watch.js:96), re-verify: page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth) <= 390 on /watch mobile. Everything else (Live TV / Movies / Series / Search / Watchlist / Favorites / Player) already passes the no-horizontal-scroll check. Mobile nav strip is correctly contained — don't break it. Movies and Search grids correctly use fluid MediaCards (no fixed-px-width regression).
rca_of_the_issue: RCA: Watch.js Row component has two render paths — loaded state (line 200-213) which correctly uses `overflow-x-auto scrollbar-thin -mx-4 sm:-mx-2 px-4 sm:px-2`, and a loading-skeleton state (line 180-189) which uses only `flex gap-3` with `shrink-0` children of fixed width w-32 (128px). With 6 skeleton items, the flex container's intrinsic width becomes ~768px on the smallest viewport, but there is NO overflow-x-auto wrapping it, so the parent <main> (which has only horizontal padding, no horizontal overflow control) inherits the wide content and pushes <body> scrollWidth to 844. Reproduction: open /watch on a 390px viewport with slow network (or fresh load before recently-added/continue-watching queries resolve) and try to scroll the page horizontally — it scrolls ~454px to the right. Mitigation 1 (preferred): add `overflow-x-auto scrollbar-thin -mx-4 sm:-mx-2 px-4 sm:px-2 pb-2` to the loading-state flex div so it matches the loaded state. Mitigation 2 (defensive): add `overflow-x-hidden` to the <main> in WatchShell so no descendant layout slip can ever leak horizontally.
